title: Reaching More Customers with Facebook Ads - Groomer to Groomer

facts.fact: Facebook offers a dozen campaign objective options for paid ads, and the choice depends on the advertiser's goal for each ad.
facts.quote: Facebook offers a dozen options to choose from when designating your campaign objective.

facts.fact: Facebook ad age targeting lets advertisers select user groups from age 13 to 65+.
facts.quote: Here you have the option of targeting user groups from age 13 to 65+.

facts.fact: The author states that with a limited budget, targeting 150,000 pet owners within a 20-mile radius spreads ad dollars thin, typically yielding an ad frequency below 1.5.
facts.quote: Targeting 150,000 pet owners within a 20-mile radius may sound fantastic. But if you’re working with a limited budget, these ad dollars will be spread thin

facts.fact: The author states that ad frequency for a narrowly targeted audience was typically less than 1.5 when targeting 150,000 pet owners in a 20-mile radius on a limited budget.
facts.quote: This means that the number of times users see your ad will be very low (typically less than 1.5).

facts.fact: The Facebook tracking pixel required for remarketing is free to create.
facts.quote: A Facebook tracking pixel must first be created (free) and placed in the source code of every page on your website

facts.fact: The author's example grooming business customer base lives within a radius of about 12 miles.
facts.quote: my customer base is primarily comprised of established professionals who live within a radius of about 12 miles

facts.fact: The author recommends excluding people who already like the business Page when running a branding campaign to avoid spending ad dollars on existing customers.
facts.quote: you may want to “exclude people who like your Page” when running a branding campaign.
